summary.headline: JK Lakshmi Cement guided FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore and sees Q1 FY27 cost pressure of INR100-130/t with limited price pass-through so far.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 industry demand growth of about 7% to roughly 480 million tonnes, with March softening to about 5% amid Middle East conflict and May sluggish before showing green shoots from 15 May. Industry capacity additions of 64 million tonnes pushed utilisation to about 69%, limiting price hikes; non-trade prices rose but trade prices lagged. Company-specific: FY26 clinker production 92.26 lakh tonnes, blended cement ratio 62%, Surat plant utilisation above 60%, and Assam limestone mining rights cancelled (INR325 crore intangible derecognised). Management expects Q1 FY27 cost inflation of about INR120-130/t, with INR300/t energy cost impact more likely in Q2, and gave no firm FY27 EBITDA/t guidance.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, as stated by analyst; management said increase was lower than peers
as cited by analyst, not disputed
Q3 was INR5.37 per analyst question; management corrected to 5.79 for Q3

segments.name: Grey cement
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 18 million tonnes; 1.35 million tonnes added in September 2025 (Surat), so FY26 average capacity was 17.7 million tonnes. No new capacity additions planned in FY27. Management benchmarks EBITDA against grey-cement peers only.

segments.name: Non-cement / building materials
segments.commentary: Q4 non-cement revenue INR169 crore, RMC INR82 crore, AAC blocks INR59 crore, margin about 4%. RMC behind plan due to deliberate focus on high-margin products; tile adhesives and plastering solutions growing well.

guidance_outlook: FY27 industry cement demand growth about 6%; company expects to grow higher than industry in FY27, citing Surat ramp-up, Udaipur and Cuttack headroom.
Q1 FY27 cost inflation about INR120-130/t, with energy cost increase about INR300/t more likely from Q2; packaging INR80-100/t; total energy and packaging about INR400/t per analyst.
Management expects to recover majority of cost increase if demand supports; petrol/diesel hike seen adding about INR15-16/t to logistics cost.

Capex FY27 about INR1,500-1,700 crore, FY28 about INR2,000 crore, FY29 about INR1,000-1,500 crore; Durg (INR3,000 crore project, about INR500 crore spent by FY26) first clinker and grinding by end-FY28; Northeast (Assam) about 1 MTPA-plus clinker and grinding about one year later (FY29); Kutch by FY30; Nagaur delayed by land and Aravalli issues.
Reasonably confident of 30 MTPA capacity by 2030 ('on course'); no firm FY27 EBITDA per tonne guidance, to be updated next quarter; expects gap to leaders to narrow by INR50-75/t in FY27.
capex_capacity: Surat plant commissioned around 22 September 2025; utilisation above 60% and expected 70%+ this year, ahead of 18-24 month ramp-up plan.

FY26 clinker utilisation about 93-94%; plan to lift blended cement ratio from 62% to about 65% and clinker utilisation to 97-98% to support growth; clinker headroom of about 7-7.5 lakh tonnes sold last year.

Two Assam mines (about 250 million tonnes reserves) secured via auction after AMDCL cancelled the MDO contract; INR130 crore AMDCL-related other non-current asset under High Court proceedings, next hearing in July.
Sirohi TSR Phase 1 complete; Phase 2 not finalised due to limited alternate fuel availability near plant.
Durg railway siding phase 2 delayed by external agencies (flyover on PWD road, SAIL track strengthening); management says no delay on its side.

NECEM (Northeast) acquisition: consideration about INR19 crore plus takeover of liabilities settled at INR12.5 crore in March; INR10 crore non-compete fee payable after completion, INR7.5 crore capital infusion (INR3.5 crore done); completion expected this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry FY26 demand growth about 7% to about 480 million tonnes; Q4 FY26 demand growth about 6-6.5%, volume about 17% QoQ; Dec-Feb growth 8-10%, March about 5%.
Industry capacity addition 64 million tonnes in FY26, national capacity 712 million tonnes; utilisation about 69%.

Prices partially recovered in non-trade segment in Q4 FY26 but not in line with cost increases; trade prices inching up. Management said May was sluggish (labour returning after elections, Middle East uncertainty) with better demand from 15 May.
Company's Q4 NSR up about 1% as its footprint (North, West, Chhattisgarh in East) saw lower price hikes; Gujarat had no initial price increase.
Non-trade market share about 42% (analyst cited); premium products growth strong; Green+ relaunched legacy brand and LC3 launched.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q1 cost pressure and how much price increase has been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR120-130/t cost increase in Q1 with INR300/t energy impact more in Q2; price hikes so far are not commensurate with cost increases, and majority recovery depends on demand.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt evolve given FY27-28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net debt will peak with capex of about INR1,500-2,000 crore, returning to normative levels once Durg EBITDA kicks in after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Can volumes grow 7-10% given 93% clinker utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow above industry in FY27 by lifting blended ratio to 65%, clinker utilisation to 97-98%, and using clinker sold last year (7-7.5 lakh tonnes).

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the NECEM liabilities and promoter payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Past liabilities of about INR12.5 crore were settled in March; INR1.5 crore paid for shares, with remaining consideration and capital infusion expected to complete this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Assam plant still viable after AMDCL cancellation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two of three mines were secured through auction (about 250 million tonnes reserves), and Northeast project proceeds based on these; capacity size slightly above 1.5 MTPA.

risks_watch: Cost inflation (energy INR300/t, packaging INR80-100/t, logistics from fuel price hike) versus limited price hikes; Q1 EBITDA/t likely to fall sharply.
Net debt rise from FY27-28 capex of about INR3,500-3,700 crore cumulative; management says peak then recovery post-Durg.
Assam/AMDCL: INR130 crore receivable recoverability tied to High Court hearing in July; Nagaur delayed by land and Aravalli Supreme Court matter.
Demand softness in May; monitor whether green shoots from mid-May hold and whether trade prices move up.
Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA per tonne; next update deferred to next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and long-term capacity targets (30 MTPA by 2030, Durg, Surat ramp-up), but evasive and cautious on near-term margins, saying EBITDA/t outlook is "quite uncertain" and deferring guidance to next quarter. Management also gave hedged answers on price recovery and was frequently disrupted by a poor audio line.

growth.why: Management expects FY27 volume growth above the industry's ~6% (industry demand guided at ~6%), backed by Surat ramp-up (utilisation above 60%, expected 70%+) and Udaipur/Cuttack headroom, with FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore; no new grey capacity in FY27, and the 30 MTPA-by-2030 target is 'reasonably confident' but Nagaur is delayed and no FY27 EBITDA/t guidance was given.
